Here’s a concise summary:

When analyzing algorithms, the running time depends on the input size (e.g., sorting 6 elements vs. 6 billion). Instead of fixed numbers, we express time as a function of input size to understand scalability. We focus on **upper bounds** (worst-case guarantees) for running time because they provide users with reliable performance expectations (e.g., "this won’t take more than 3 seconds"). Lower bounds (e.g., "it takes *at least* 3 seconds") are less useful, as they don’t cap the runtime and offer no practical guarantee.
